_meta.title: An example candidate, served for the intake form
_meta.note: One illustrative Sri Lankan project, served to pre-fill the intake form so a presenter can show a candidate coming in with every field already carrying its evidence tier. It is served, never recorded: pressing Record is what records it, under the caller's own organisation, and a second press updates the same record in place. Not DFCC's figures.
_meta.provenanceSource: Example values entered by Datum Solutions — illustrative; edit to the confirmed figures before any submission.

project.name: Tea Factory Biomass Boiler Conversion and Rooftop Solar
project.sector: Industrial energy efficiency and fuel switching
project.selectionReason: A credit line for regional tea factories to replace furnace-oil boilers with certified biomass boilers and add rooftop solar for withering and drying, where the fuel bill is the factory's largest controllable cost and the payback exceeds the tenor local lenders offer.
project.essNote: Works within existing factory premises. Biomass is sourced from certified fuelwood plantations, with air-quality and sourcing conditions carried in the ESMP.

financing.gcfInstrumentDetail: A concessional tranche on-lent through DFCC to stretch tenor to the boiler's life. No grant element.

viabilityWithoutGcf.reason: On a five-year commercial tenor the boiler conversion does not clear the factory's debt-service cover; the GCF tranche buys the years of tenor the payback needs, not a margin subsidy.

annual_tCO2e.method: furnace oil displaced x emission factor, net of biomass supply-chain emissions; rooftop generation x grid emission factor

baseline.description: Furnace-oil boilers and grid electricity for withering and drying at the participating factories
baseline.counterfactual: Without the credit line the factories continue on furnace oil and grid power

indirect.definition: Estate workers and smallholder green-leaf suppliers to the participating factories

risks.description: Biomass supply falls short of the boilers’ demand in the dry months, pushing factories back to furnace oil.
risks.mitigation: Supply agreements with two certified fuelwood plantations per factory, with a minimum-stock covenant in the loan terms.

risks.description: Tea auction prices fall and factories cannot service the converted-boiler loan.
risks.mitigation: Debt-service cover tested at a 20% price fall at appraisal; a one-year grace period on principal.

risks.description: Particulate emissions from biomass combustion exceed the air-quality standard at factories near settlements.
risks.mitigation: Cyclone separators specified in the boiler standard; the ESMP carries the emission limit and the monitoring.

implementation.arrangements: DFCC on-lends the GCF tranche to participating factories through its regional branches; a technical partner appraises each boiler conversion against the specification, and the factory owner contracts the installer.
implementation.governance: A steering committee — DFCC sustainability unit, the technical partner and the Planters’ Association — meets quarterly; the executing entity reports to it and to the Fund through DFCC.
implementation.procurementApproach: Factories procure boilers from a pre-qualified supplier list under DFCC’s procurement policy; the technical partner is procured by open tender.

timetable.milestone: Technical partner appointed and boiler specification published
First twenty factories appraised and financed
Remaining factories financed; rooftop solar commissioned
Final commissioning and closure of the credit line

sustainability.strategy: The fuel saving repays the loan within the boiler’s life, so the conversion pays for itself; the pre-qualified supplier list and the boiler specification stay with the Planters’ Association after closure.
sustainability.exitStrategy: The GCF tranche is repaid through DFCC over the loan tenor; no further concessional funding is needed once the converted factories are operating.
sustainability.ownershipAfterClosure: Each factory owns its boiler and rooftop installation; DFCC holds the loans to maturity.
sustainability.financialSustainability: Operating cost falls by the fuel-oil bill less biomass and maintenance; the model shows debt-service cover above 1.3x at the appraisal price.

stakeholders.name: Planters’ Association of Ceylon
stakeholders.outcome: Endorsed the credit line; asked that the boiler specification be published before the first appraisal.

stakeholders.name: Ministry of Environment — Climate Change Secretariat
stakeholders.outcome: Informed of the concept; confirmed the NDC 3.0 industrial sector target it serves.

stakeholders.name: Estate worker representatives, Nuwara Eliya
stakeholders.outcome: Raised air quality near factory housing; the emission limit and monitoring were added to the ESMP.

financialTerms.securityPackage: Charge over the boiler and rooftop installation; corporate guarantee of the factory owner.
financialTerms.onLendingTerms: On-lent in rupees at DFCC’s cost of the tranche plus a 2% margin, tenor matched to the boiler’s life.

disbursements.condition: Technical partner appointed; first ten loans approved

monitoring.arrangements: The technical partner reads each factory’s fuel-oil and biomass purchases and the rooftop generation meter quarterly; DFCC consolidates them into the annual performance report.

indicators.method: Fuel-oil displaced × emission factor, net of biomass supply-chain emissions; rooftop generation × grid factor
indicators.verification: Fuel invoices and meter readings, sampled by DFCC internal audit

indicators.method: Stack test against the ESMP limit

monitoring.evaluationPlan: A mid-term review after the first twenty factories; a final evaluation within a year of closure, by an independent evaluator DFCC engages.
monitoring.reportingSchedule: Quarterly to the steering committee; annually to the Fund through the annual performance report.
